rows.why: S1 depends on the default share being 7500 bps, which gives 7500 of 10000. No item asks what the default share is. Item 3 covers whether a configured share is valid, and item 1 covers rounding. Neither one decides the default value.

Item 1 asks how an uneven share is rounded. The pick rounds the hidden-test part down with exact BigInt division and gives the remainder to the UAT release. That yields 749 and 250, exact up to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, as the scenario expects.
Item 9 asks how the UAT release amount is computed. The pick releases the bounty minus earlier releases, which is the remaining balance the scenario expects.
Item 10 asks what a failed hidden-test run does. The pick returns the current state without writing, so nothing is recorded and the task stays locked.

Item 6 asks what happens when UAT is approved before the hidden tests pass. The pick rejects with an Error and stores nothing, which matches the refusal. The pick doesn't give the error message, but the behaviour agrees.
Item 5 asks what a bounty of 0 does. The pick records releases of amount 0, but the scenario says no release is ever recorded. The 'pro bono' status matches, the recording does not.

Item 7 asks what happens when hidden tests pass again after the first release. The pick ignores any later pass event, whatever its id, and writes nothing. That covers both the repeat of e1 and a different pass event.

Item 11 asks how concurrent events are handled. The pick runs events one at a time through a per-store queue. The second event then sees the first release and records nothing (items 7 and 8), so exactly one release is recorded for both event kinds.
Item 12 asks what a store write failure does. The pick rejects with the store's error, records nothing, and leaves the event retryable, which matches the scenario.
